newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index hits year low in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index hits year low in thin trading.

text.p: The Slovak SAX index slipped to a new year low in thin trading activity on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday with brokers seeing volatility and instability in the short and medium term.
The 16-share SAX index fell to 170.85 points.
"What we see is high volatility all around the issues, and nobody can seriously say where are the real share prices are at the moment," Radovan Dzugas of Creditranstalt said.
The BSE has been in constant decline since the country's money market was paralysed by foreign speculation in April and May.
Steel maker VSZ traded the biggest volume on the bourse's listed floor, of 164 shares, closing unchanged at 625 crowns. Most of the remaining major issues fell in light trading.
Overall, volume increased to 277,632 shares, from 249,442 shares traded on Wednesday, while turnover eased to 73.77 million crowns, from 89.46 million.
